articles.title: Log Kya Kahenge: The Committee That Does Not Exist
articles.titleHinglish: Log Kya Kahenge: Wo Committee Jo Hai Hi Nahi
articles.content:
Three words have redirected more Indian lives than any career counsellor: log kya kahenge. Careers dropped, marriages entered, cities not moved to, all decided by an audience nobody has ever actually met.

Start with the obvious thing that is still worth saying plainly. The log in log kya kahenge are not a committee. They are relatives who will discuss you for two evenings, neighbours who will forget within a month, and a few people who genuinely enjoy other people's failures and would have found something regardless. None of them will be present at the end of your life, in the job you dislike, or in the marriage you were persuaded into. You will be. Alone.

But it is lazy to stop there, because the fear is not stupid. In a society where family reputation genuinely affects a sister's marriage prospects, a father's standing, and how a family is treated in a small town, social judgement has real costs. Anyone who tells you it is all imaginary has probably never lived in a place where it is not.

So the useful question is not how to stop caring. It is: whose opinion has actually earned a vote?

Make the list small and concrete. A person gets a vote if they will be there for the consequences of the decision — they will help if it fails, they will be affected by it either way, and they know the details of your life rather than a summary. By that standard, most of the committee vanishes immediately. A distant uncle who will comment at a wedding and then go home has an opinion, not a stake.

Notice too who is actually being protected. Often the sentence log kya kahenge really means I am afraid of being judged for how my child turned out. That is worth compassion — your parents' fear is genuine, and in their generation the cost of standing out was higher. Compassion, though, is not the same as obedience. You can be gentle with the fear and still not let it decide your life.

A practical move: separate the private decision from the public announcement. Many family conflicts are not about the choice at all but about how the news travels. Deciding calmly, then letting your parents tell the story in their own words, in their own time, removes ninety percent of the heat from the average situation.

And remember the arithmetic almost nobody does. The people whose opinions you fear are, at this exact moment, worrying about what people are saying about them. Everybody is starring in their own anxiety and appearing briefly as an extra in everyone else's. It is not a stadium watching you. It is a corridor of people looking at their own feet.
articles.contentHinglish:
Teen shabdon ne kisi bhi career counsellor se zyada Indian zindagiyan mod di hain: log kya kahenge. Career chhode gaye, shaadiyan hui, sheher nahi badle — sab ek aisi audience ke liye jise kabhi kisi ne mila hi nahi.

Seedhi baat pehle, jise phir bhi saaf bolna zaroori hai. "Log kya kahenge" wale log koi committee nahi hain. Wo rishtedaar hain jo do shaam aapke baare mein baat karenge, padosi hain jo mahine bhar mein bhool jaayenge, aur kuch log hain jinhe doosron ki asafalta mein sach mein mazaa aata hai aur jinhe kuch na kuch mil hi jaata. Inme se koi bhi aapki zindagi ke ant mein maujood nahi hoga, na us job mein jo aapko pasand nahi, na us shaadi mein jisme aapko manaya gaya tha. Aap honge. Akele.

Par yahin ruk jaana aalasi baat hai, kyunki yeh dar bewakoof nahi hai. Jis samaj mein khandan ki izzat sach mein behen ke rishton, papa ke rutbe, aur chhote sheher mein khandan ke saath hone wale bartav ko affect karti ho, wahan samaj ka faisla asli keemat rakhta hai. Jo kehta hai yeh sab kaalpanik hai, wo shayad kabhi aisi jagah raha hi nahi jahan yeh sach hota hai.

Toh kaam ka sawaal yeh nahi ki parwaah karna kaise band karein. Sawaal yeh hai: kiski raay ne sach mein vote kamaya hai?

List chhoti aur specific rakho. Vote us insaan ka hai jo faisle ke nateeje mein saath khada hoga — jo fail hone par madad karega, jise dono soorat mein farq padega, aur jo aapki zindagi ki detail jaanta hai, sirf summary nahi. Is paimane par zyadatar committee turant gayab ho jaati hai. Wo door ke chacha jo shaadi mein comment karke ghar chale jaayenge — unki raay hai, hissa nahi.

Yeh bhi dekho ki asal mein bachaya kise ja raha hai. Aksar "log kya kahenge" ka matlab hota hai — mujhe dar hai ki mere bachche ki wajah se mujhe judge kiya jaayega. Us par taras aana chahiye — aapke maa-baap ka dar asli hai, aur unki peedhi mein alag dikhne ki keemat zyada thi. Par taras aur hukum maanna alag cheezein hain. Aap us dar ke saath narmi kar sakte ho aur phir bhi use apni zindagi ka faisla nahi karne de sakte.

Ek practical cheez: private faisle ko public announcement se alag karo. Ghar ke bahut se jhagde faisle ke baare mein hote hi nahi, wo is baare mein hote hain ki khabar kaise failegi. Shaant hokar faisla lena aur phir maa-baap ko apne shabdon mein, apne waqt par kahani sunane dena — aam haalat mein isse nabbe percent garmi utar jaati hai.

Aur wo hisaab yaad rakho jo lagbhag koi nahi karta. Jin logon ki raay se aap darte ho, wo is waqt yahi soch rahe hain ki unke baare mein log kya keh rahe honge. Har koi apni hi ghabraahat ka hero hai aur doosron ki kahani mein sirf ek chhota sa extra. Yeh stadium nahi hai jo aapko dekh raha hai. Yeh ek corridor hai jisme sab apne hi pairon ko dekh rahe hain.

articles.title: Boundaries With Parents Without Declaring War
articles.titleHinglish: Maa-Baap Ke Saath Boundary, Bina Jung Ke
articles.content:
Most advice about boundaries was written for a culture where children leave at eighteen and the family becomes optional. That advice does not survive contact with an Indian household, where you may be thirty-two, financially independent, and still expected to answer for coming home at midnight.

So here is the version that works where love, money, duty and living space are all tangled together.

Start by separating the two things people confuse. Respect is what you give — how you speak, whether you shout, whether you remain warm. Compliance is what you do — the career, the marriage, the timing, the city. In most Indian homes these two have been welded together, so any disagreement feels like disrespect. Pulling them apart is the entire skill. I love you, I am not shouting at you, and my answer is still no is a complete sentence, and it takes practice mostly because it feels illegal.

Do not fight for permission you were never going to receive. This is the most common mistake. People stay in a two-hour argument trying to make their parents say yes and approve, when the realistic outcome is that parents accept slowly, over months, after the fact. Waiting for enthusiastic approval before acting keeps you frozen for years. Inform, do not negotiate, on the decisions that are genuinely yours.

Keep the boundary narrow. Not you must stop interfering in my life, which is a declaration of war, but I will not discuss marriage at dinner. One specific behaviour, one specific limit. Broad boundaries produce broad fights; narrow ones are survivable and hold better.

Expect the escalation and do not read it as failure. When a pattern that has run for decades is interrupted, the volume goes up before it goes down — more calls, more guilt, sometimes a relative deployed as a messenger. That is the system testing whether the change is real. Holding the same calm line three or four times does more than any speech ever will.

Money deserves its own sentence. If they support you financially, some influence is real and pretending otherwise is dishonest. This is one reason financial independence matters more than any argument you could win. Independence does not buy love; it buys the right to disagree without a crisis.

And keep the relationship fed while you hold the line. The reason boundaries feel brutal in Indian families is that they often arrive along with distance — fewer calls, shorter visits, colder tone. Try the opposite: hold the boundary and increase the warmth. Call more, not less. Ask about their day. Show up for the things that matter to them.

What you are aiming for is not victory. It is a version of the relationship where you can be fully yourself and still be in the room. That takes years, and it is worth them.
articles.contentHinglish:
Boundaries ki zyadatar salaah us culture ke liye likhi gayi hai jahan bachche atharah saal mein ghar chhod dete hain aur family optional ho jaati hai. Wo salaah Indian ghar se takra ke bikhar jaati hai, jahan aap battis saal ke, apne paison par khade ho sakte ho aur phir bhi raat baarah baje ghar aane ka jawab dena padta hai.

Toh yeh wo version hai jo wahan chalta hai jahan pyaar, paisa, farz aur ek hi chhat sab uljhe hue hain.

Do cheezein alag karke shuru karo jinhe log mila dete hain. Izzat wo hai jo aap dete ho — kaise bolte ho, chillate ho ya nahi, garmjoshi bachi hai ya nahi. Compliance wo hai jo aap karte ho — career, shaadi, timing, sheher. Zyadatar Indian gharon mein yeh dono welding karke jod diye gaye hain, isliye koi bhi asehmati be-izzati lagti hai. Inhe alag karna hi poora hunar hai. "Main aapse pyaar karta hoon, main chilla nahi raha, aur mera jawab phir bhi na hai" — yeh poora sentence hai, aur iski practice isliye lagti hai kyunki yeh gair-kanooni sa mehsoos hota hai.

Us ijazat ke liye mat lado jo milni hi nahi thi. Yeh sabse aam galti hai. Log do ghante ki bahas mein lage rehte hain ki maa-baap haan bhi bolein aur khush bhi hon, jabki asli nateeja yeh hota hai ki maa-baap dheere dheere, mahino mein, hone ke baad sweekar karte hain. Kaam shuru karne se pehle khush-dili wali manzoori ka intezaar aapko saalon jamaa deta hai. Jo faisle sach mein aapke hain, unme bata do — mol-bhav mat karo.

Boundary ko chhota rakho. "Aap meri zindagi mein dakhal dena band karo" nahi — wo jung ka elaan hai — balki "main dinner par shaadi ki baat nahi karunga". Ek specific behaviour, ek specific limit. Badi boundaries badi ladai laati hain; chhoti wali jhel jaati hain aur zyada tikti hain.

Awaaz oonchi hogi, use haar mat samajhna. Jab dashkon purana pattern rukta hai to volume pehle badhta hai, phir girta hai — zyada calls, zyada guilt, kabhi kabhi koi rishtedaar sandeshvaahak banke. Yeh system check kar raha hai ki badlav asli hai ya nahi. Teen-chaar baar wahi shaant line dohra dena kisi bhi bhaashan se zyada kaam karta hai.

Paise ka apna alag sentence hai. Agar wo aapko paise se support karte hain, to unka kuch asar asli hai aur ise jhutlana beimaani hai. Yahi ek wajah hai ki financial independence kisi bhi jeeti hui bahas se zyada mayne rakhti hai. Independence pyaar nahi khareedti; wo bina crisis ke asehmat hone ka haq khareedti hai.

Aur line pakadte hue rishte ko khaana dete raho. Indian gharon mein boundaries itni kadwi isliye lagti hain kyunki wo aksar doori ke saath aati hain — kam calls, chhoti visits, thanda tone. Ulta karke dekho: boundary rakho aur garmjoshi badha do. Zyada call karo, kam nahi. Unka din poochho. Jo unke liye mayne rakhta hai wahan maujood raho.

Aapka target jeet nahi hai. Target rishte ka wo version hai jahan aap poori tarah apne aap ho sako aur phir bhi us kamre mein raho. Ismein saal lagte hain, aur wo saal iske laayak hain.

articles.title: Sharma Ji Ka Beta: Growing Up Compared
articles.titleHinglish: Sharma Ji Ka Beta: Tulna Mein Bade Hona
articles.content:
Almost every Indian child grows up next to an invisible sibling — a cousin with better marks, a neighbour's son with a government job, someone's daughter who did everything on time. You were never introduced, but you competed with them for two decades.

Parents who do this are rarely being cruel. Most of them genuinely believe comparison is fuel: point at someone better, and the child will rise. Some of them were raised the same way and are simply repeating what they know. Understanding that helps, but it does not undo what comparison actually builds.

What it builds is a person who cannot enjoy their own achievements. When success is defined by a ranking, arriving somewhere good gives you about ten minutes of relief before you look sideways to see who is further ahead. Nothing is ever enough, because the standard is not a level — it is a position relative to whoever is doing best this year.

It builds something else too: a habit of hiding. Children who are compared learn to under-report — the failed test, the rejection, the thing they are struggling with — because information becomes ammunition. Twenty years later the same person still does not tell their family when things go wrong, and everyone wonders why they seem distant.

So what can you actually do about it now, as an adult?

Stop arguing about the comparison. When it is made, you do not have to prove that the cousin's job is worse or that his salary is exaggerated. You can decline the frame entirely: I am not going to compare my life to his. Said calmly, repeatedly, without heat. You will not win the debate, but you can stop participating in it.

Then check where you have internalised it. This is the harder part. Most people who hated being compared grow up to do it constantly, silently, on LinkedIn and Instagram, with far more precision than any relative managed. The relative has stopped. You have not. Noticing that the voice is now yours is the beginning of turning it off.

Measure against your own past. It sounds like a poster, but it is mechanically better: the question am I better than I was two years ago is answerable, and the answer is under your control. Am I better than him is neither.

And if you have children, or will, know that the alternative to comparison is not the absence of standards. You can expect a great deal without ever naming another child. Expectation says I believe you can do this. Comparison says someone else is the proof that you are not enough. Children hear the difference, and they carry whichever one they were given for a very long time.
articles.contentHinglish:
Lagbhag har Indian bachcha ek anadekhe bhai-behen ke bagal mein bada hota hai — koi cousin jiske marks behtar hain, padosi ka beta jiski sarkari naukri hai, kisi ki beti jisne sab kuch time par kar liya. Aapka parichay kabhi nahi hua, par aap unse do dashak tak lade.

Jo maa-baap aisa karte hain wo aksar zaalim nahi hote. Zyadatar sach mein maante hain ki tulna petrol hai: kisi behtar ki taraf ishaara karo aur bachcha upar uthega. Kuch ko khud aise hi paala gaya tha aur wo bas wahi dohra rahe hain. Yeh samajhna madad karta hai, par jo tulna banati hai use mitaata nahi.

Wo banati hai aisa insaan jo apni hi kaamyabi ka mazaa nahi le sakta. Jab safalta ki paribhasha ranking ho, to kisi achhi jagah pahunchne par lagbhag dus minute ki raahat milti hai aur phir nazar bagal mein chali jaati hai ki aur aage kaun hai. Kuch bhi kabhi kaafi nahi hota, kyunki paimana koi level nahi hai — wo is saal ke sabse aage wale ke saapeksh ek position hai.

Wo ek aur cheez bhi banati hai: chhupane ki aadat. Jin bachchon ki tulna hoti hai wo kam batana seekh lete hain — fail hua test, reject hua application, wo cheez jisme dikkat aa rahi hai — kyunki information hathiyaar ban jaati hai. Bees saal baad wahi insaan ab bhi ghar mein nahi batata jab kuch galat hota hai, aur sab sochte hain yeh itna door door kyun rehta hai.

Toh ab, bade hone ke baad, kiya kya ja sakta hai?

Tulna par bahas karna band karo. Jab tulna ho, aapko yeh sabit karne ki zaroorat nahi ki cousin ki job kharab hai ya uski salary badha chadha ke batayi ja rahi hai. Aap poora frame hi mana kar sakte ho: main apni zindagi ki tulna uski zindagi se nahi karunga. Shaant awaaz mein, baar baar, bina garmi ke. Aap bahas nahi jeetoge, par usme hissa lena band kar sakte ho.

Phir dekho ki aapne isse kahan andar utaar liya hai. Yahi mushkil hissa hai. Jinhe tulna se nafrat thi, wo bade hokar lagataar, chupchaap, LinkedIn aur Instagram par yahi karte hain — kisi rishtedaar se kahin zyada precision ke saath. Rishtedaar ab ruk chuka hai. Aap nahi ruke. Yeh notice kar lena ki awaaz ab aapki apni hai — usse band karne ki shuruaat wahi hai.

Apne hi ateet se naapo. Poster jaisa lagta hai, par technically behtar hai: "kya main do saal pehle se behtar hoon" ka jawab mil sakta hai, aur wo jawab aapke haath mein hai. "Kya main usse behtar hoon" — na jawab milta hai, na haath mein hai.

Aur agar aapke bachche hain ya honge, to yaad rakhna ki tulna ka vikalp "koi ummeed hi na rakhna" nahi hai. Aap bahut kuch chah sakte ho bina kisi doosre bachche ka naam liye. Ummeed kehti hai — mujhe yakeen hai tum yeh kar sakte ho. Tulna kehti hai — koi aur iska saboot hai ki tum kaafi nahi ho. Bachche is farq ko sunte hain, aur jo mila hota hai use bahut lambe waqt tak uthaye rehte hain.
